$comment: Deploy progress: how far a deploy, update, restart or reboot has come, from the click to the first render on the new code. docs/deploy-progress.md is the prose, docs/deploy-progress-fixtures.json the conformance corpus. Generated tables: frameos/tools/generate_deploy_progress_contract.py (run after every edit). A kind is one ordered list of stages; the control plane advances to the stages it performs itself (source: control-plane) and folds the device's own signals into the rest (source: device/queue). The record lives on the frame row as `deploy_progress` on both control planes.

record.$comment: The shape of frame.deploy_progress. `at` moves on every change; `progress` is bytes while the device downloads; `error` is set only with status=error.

fields.id: string: the deploy's id (the task id the browser minted, or the command id / uuid the control plane minted)
fields.stage: string: one of the kind's stages, or `done`
fields.detail: string | null: one short sentence about the current step, for the bar's caption
fields.progress: {current, total} | null: bytes so far, while a download or upload reports them
fields.version: string | null: the FrameOS release this deploy installs, when known
fields.at: ISO timestamp of the last change

signals.$comment: The closed vocabulary of things that move a record. `control-plane:<stage>` is the plane's own step (the backend task, the cloud route or hub). Everything else is observed: a device log line, a command-queue state change, a hub session event.
signals.control-plane: control-plane:<stage>  the control plane reached that stage of its own work

device.bootup: the runtime's `bootup` log line (Linux and ESP32); on the cloud the hub's hello (session start) is the same signal
device.reload: the Linux runtime's `reload` log line: it re-read frame.json and the scenes and will render
device.render:done: the runtime finished a render (`render:done`); on the cloud the device's `render` announce is the same signal
device.ota:waiting: ESP32 `ota:<plane>` status `waiting`: a render pass finishes before the download
device.ota:verified: ESP32 `ota:<plane>` status `verified`: installed, restarting into it
device.ota:up-to-date: ESP32 `ota:<plane>` status `up-to-date` / `skipped` / `downgrade-refused`: nothing to install, the frame restarts on what it has

queue.command:sent:<type>: the hub wrote the verb to the device socket
queue.command:acked:<type>: the device acked the verb (set_scenes and set_settings on the backend: the pull reported the ETags the backend serves)
queue.commands:settled: every row of this deploy is acked (the backend's deploy_commands_settled)
queue.scene_ack: cloud: the device reports the assigned scene set is live (`scene_ack` with the assigned checksum)

stages.$comment: Every stage a kind may use. `staleAfterSeconds` is how long the record may sit in the stage with no change before the workspace stops believing it (the bar hides, the row goes back to `last seen`). The runners never expire a record themselves: `at` is what the reader compares.

queued.label: queued
queued.description: The job is on the worker queue (backend) or the verb is on the frame's command queue (cloud); nothing has happened yet.

connecting.label: connecting
connecting.description: SSH / Remote session to the frame, distro probe, deploy plan.

building.label: building
building.description: Getting the FrameOS binary: the precompiled release (download, signature check), a cross-compile, or an on-device build.

uploading.label: uploading
uploading.description: Release directory, binary, scenes and settings, vendor files on their way to the frame.

installing.label: installing
installing.description: FrameOS stopped, `frameos setup` running (drivers, services, release activation), fonts synced, cleanup.

restarting.label: restarting
restarting.description: The service restart or device reboot was issued; waiting for the runtime to come back.

reloading.label: reloading
reloading.description: The runtime was asked to re-read its files in place (no restart).

saving.label: saving on the frame
saving.description: Service keys, settings and scenes posted to the frame's admin API (the device's own Save).

waiting.label: waiting for the frame
waiting.description: Queued for a frame that is asleep or off; it takes the work on its next check-in. Not stale while the frame's next wake (plus record.wakeGraceSeconds) is still ahead.

sending.label: sending
sending.description: The hub is streaming the verb to the connected frame.

downloading.label: downloading
downloading.description: The device is fetching the release image / archive.

verified.label: installed
verified.description: The device verified and installed the release; it restarts into it.

flashing.label: flashing
flashing.description: The browser is writing the image over USB.

booting.label: booting
booting.description: Waiting for the runtime's bootup line on the new code.

receiving.label: receiving scenes
receiving.description: The frame is pulling its scenes and settings (after the boot, on an ESP32).

loading.label: loading scenes
loading.description: The frame accepted the scenes and is making them live.

rendering.label: first render
rendering.description: Waiting for the first render on the new code / scenes.

kinds.$comment: `stages` is the ordered list a bar is drawn from. Each entry: `stage`, optional `on` (signal -> next stage, or `done` / `error`), optional `holdOn` (signals that refresh `at` and `progress` without leaving the stage). A control plane advances with `control-plane:<stage>` only forward along the list; an observed signal the current stage does not list is ignored, so a late line from the previous runtime cannot move the record.

linux_full.label: Deploy FrameOS, scenes & settings
linux_full.frames: Linux frames the backend reaches over SSH or the FrameOS Remote (rpios, buildroot with a shell).

linux_fast.label: Deploy scenes & settings
linux_fast.frames: Linux frames the backend reaches over SSH or the FrameOS Remote; the binary stays, frame.json and the scenes are replaced and the runtime reloads (or restarts, when setup or TLS asks for it).

admin_push.label: Deploy over the admin API
admin_push.frames: Linux frames the backend only reaches over their admin HTTP API (an adopted generic Buildroot card: no Remote, no SSH). Fast and full deploys are the same push.

esp32_full.label: Deploy firmware, scenes & settings
esp32_full.frames: ESP32 frames on the backend: the scenes and settings rows go on the command queue, the board installs the signed release over the air, boots, pulls the rows, renders.

esp32_fast.label: Deploy scenes & settings
esp32_fast.frames: ESP32 frames on the backend: the scenes and settings rows go on the command queue; the board pulls them on its next pass (nudged if awake) and renders.

esp32_usb.label: Deploy over USB
esp32_usb.frames: ESP32 frames flashed or provisioned from the browser over USB. The control plane learns of it when the flasher reports completion; the board then boots and renders.

virtual.label: Render
virtual.frames: Virtual frames: deploying is rendering, on the backend itself.

upgrade.label: Update FrameOS
upgrade.frames: Linux frames upgrading themselves (the runtime's signed release upgrade): asked over the admin API (backend) or by the notify_update_available verb (cloud). Progress is the runtime's cloud:upgrade lines, then the boot and the first render.

firmware.label: Update firmware
firmware.frames: ESP32 frames installing the signed release over the air without a scene deploy: the notify_update_available verb (queued on either plane), the device's ota lines, its bootup / hello on the new release, its first render.

cloud_scenes.label: Push scenes
cloud_scenes.frames: Every cloud frame: the set_scenes verb from queued through the device's scene_ack to its first render announce.

restart.label: Restart FrameOS
restart.frames: Every frame: the runtime exits and comes back (an ESP32 reboots the chip).

reboot.label: Reboot device
reboot.frames: Every frame: the whole device restarts.
